selection: The pre-repair shipping source was compiled natively on Apple arm64. From each of -89.5, -86, -82.5, -79, -75.5, -72, -68.5 and -65, the search stepped upward one double at a time to the first apparent altitude whose normal-mode correction was zero while both adjacent doubles returned a nonzero correction. The ninth altitude is the reviewed example -69.32021918360232. Each altitude is followed by its next lower and next higher double.

expectations.preRepair: Every child returns. Each normal-mode straddle altitude returns zero direct correction, and its horizontal vector equals the no-refraction vector for the same altitude and model.
expectations.repaired: Every child returns. Each normal-mode straddle altitude returns a nonzero direct correction equal bit-for-bit to the correction at one of its adjacent doubles, and its horizontal vector differs from the no-refraction vector. Every other payload matches the pre-repair record bit-for-bit.
expectations.bounds: Apple arm64 libm selected these altitudes. The records establish the repair for this population on this platform, not for every double or platform.

plannedRepair: When the inverse iteration alternates between two adjacent doubles, return the lower one instead of zero. Wider two-state cycles, stalls, nonfinite iterations and the 1,000-iteration limit still return zero. Converged results, the residual expression, the 1e-14 comparison and the forward model are unchanged.
